A wave travels from the body out along every chain (spine, neck and head, dorsal strand, tail, kelp horns, every wing strand, feelers, arms): each joint bends about X and, a quarter cycle later, about Z (ZR as much), so the strands ripple and trace small loops; joint k is k*LAG of the loop behind and (1 + GROW*k) times the chain amplitude. Old text: 160 frames x 30 ms = 4.8 s. One sway sw(t), CYC=2 per loop (2.4 s each): the body rocks SWAY deg (and rolls ROLL a quarter cycle later), and every chain trails it - each link LAG of the loop later and a bit bigger than the one before (neck, head, horns; wing roots and strands root to tip; feelers, arms, tail). The whole sprite floats FLOAT px once per loop (broad crest, quick trough: wave). Whole cycles only, so frame 160 = frame 0.
